A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including the revised proofs and new numerical tables. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical results, proofs, and a mathematical lower-bound example, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: Appendix E and Tables 1–4 report original numerical contraction tests on Markov kernels and random directions. These qualify despite the checklist's inconsistent statement that the paper contains no experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same geometric truncation, MLMC correction, anchored value updates, and subsequent average-reward estimation phase. Added block-ending statements clarify the pseudocode without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: v3 introduces empirical coverage absent from v2: four cyclic ergodic kernels with 5–8 states, evaluated individually and under contamination, TV, and Wasserstein-1 uncertainty. These uncertainty types were already studied theoretically; their numerical evaluation in Appendix E is new.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 introduce the span seminorm as an explicitly reported comparator for the constructed seminorms' contraction behavior. No competing policy-evaluation algorithm is empirically benchmarked.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces numerical protocols: 1,000 random directions per fixed kernel, and 30 sampled kernels with 50 directions each per robust case. The robust tests use radius 0.15 and a finite-product norm approximation with maximum length 3 and 25 products per length. v2 has no corresponding evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New analyses test the one-step contraction underlying Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2, including all three uncertainty families. They compare sampled contraction ratios with the stated contraction factors and span behavior; v2 provides proofs without these numerical checks.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports minimum, median, 90th-percentile, and maximum contraction ratios across sampled directions and kernels. These are descriptive distribution summaries; neither version supplies repeated-experiment uncertainty, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 add sixteen numerical result rows absent from v2. Fixed-kernel maximum ratios are 0.8090, 0.8718, 0.9014, and 0.8685; robust-case maxima range from 0.8134 to 0.9162, while reported maximum span ratios equal 1. These are new diagnostic findings, not improvements over earlier learning-performance measurements.

T1.justification: v3 replaces all-kernel ergodicity with nominal-model ergodicity plus explicit radius conditions, substantially revising v2's existing small-radius discussion. Appendix A adds Dobrushin product bounds and joint-spectral-radius arguments; Lemma F.1 corrects v2's identification of joint spectral radius with the maximum individual spectral radius. It also revises the Lyapunov-series convergence proof and changes the stated TV Lipschitz factor from 1 to 1+1/delta in Lemma 5.3.

C1.justification: The headline claims of first finite-sample policy evaluation and order-optimal epsilon dependence remain. The introduction now foregrounds nominal-model ergodicity in its contribution statement. Since v2 already discussed this relaxation for small radii in Remark 1 and Appendix B, this is a limited reframing rather than an entirely new contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly leaves tight dependence on S, A, and the contraction factor open, explains the types of model mismatch represented by each uncertainty set, and interprets the new numerical checks as supporting contraction. The existing ergodicity and function-approximation limitations remain, with applicability further qualified by the revised radius conditions.

D1.justification: Appendix E supplies kernel formulas, numerical parameter choices, sampling budgets, and the finite-product approximation used to evaluate the seminorms. These are new implementation disclosures for the diagnostics. Code access, hardware, seeds, and complete uncertainty-sampling instructions are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of concurrent finite-sample work by Chen, Wang, and Si and two Roch-led studies, distinguishing the paper's policy-evaluation focus. It also expands citations on average-reward RL, uncertainty models, and applications, and revises the characterization of prior policy-optimization oracle access. This substantively updates positioning beyond relocating v2's related work.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, the ergodicity assumption moves earlier, appendix organization changes, and a conference checklist is added. Copyediting and terminology are refined, but most existing abstract, exposition, and algorithm descriptions remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reformats the document into the NeurIPS style, changing the title and author block, text and equation layout, and pseudocode presentation. It also introduces four captioned numerical tables; v2 has no corresponding result displays.

improvement.justification: Correcting the individual-versus-joint spectral-radius identity and adding explicit product-contraction arguments address an important weakness in v2's central proof. Revised radius conditions, Lyapunov-series reasoning, and numerical checks substantially strengthen the paper's theoretical support. The numerical checks remain approximate and the checklist incorrectly denies experiments, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the central proof improvements.
